medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
INMED
Since 1973, Indians Into Medicine has assisted Indigenous students in pursuing a career in health care. Over 250 Indigenous physicians and over 500 Indigenous health professionals have graduated from UND as a result.

DIVERSITY STATEMENT:
The University of North Dakota and its School of Medicine and Health Sciences takes pride in their mission to meet the individual and group needs of a diverse and pluralistic society through education, research, and service.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence are permitted for educational, personal, and other reasons; must be approved by the school's Medical Student Academic Performance Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are many ways for students to be involved. Extracurricular activities such as: the Malpractice Bowl (a flag football competition against the Law School), student government, medical school awards gala, special interest groups, intramural sports, and other volunteer opportunities. Our medical students have over 35 student organizations and they are very active.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: In addition to its main campus in Grand Forks, ND the UND School of Medicine & Health Sciences maintains campus offices in Bismarck, Fargo, and Minot. Students complete the first 20 months on the main campus and their clinical instruction on one of the four campuses.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The UND Apartment Community includes over 600 conveniently located apartments. They are especially proud of our diverse population and enjoy serving UND students, families, and faculty pursuing education and research on campus. Other rental housing is available throughout the community too.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: In an effort to support the LGBTQ+ community, UND offers LGBTQ+ training for faculty and staff. Making Campus Safe for LGBTQ+ Students training explores the challenges faced by LGBTQ+ students and provides ways that educators can help create a safe and respectful campus environment.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Accommodations are frequently provided after meeting with our Office of Student Disability Resources.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: We have an Associate Dean for Wellness, as well as two full-time Wellness Advocates that are dedicated to our medical students. They put on mandatory sessions to help maintain emotional, physical, and spiritual wellness. They offer many other opportunities for improving the different areas of wellness. They are on call 24/7 for any student issues that arise or need immediate assistance.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At the University of North Dakota School of Medicine and Health Sciences, student input is a primary driver in building and maintaining a medical school experience where students feel valued, included, and supported. We believe in the power of interprofessional learning and embed interprofessional experiences across each of our health programs, allowing our medical students to work directly with our physical and occupational therapy students, social work students, nursing students, and other future providers. These experiences have been developed to strengthen the healthcare teams that our students will lead in their future roles as physicians. Through our patient-centered curriculum and health simulation program, UND’s medical students are challenged daily and leave our program prepared for anything they might experience in their careers.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: Student Success and Well-Being. We have an in house counselor for our students, she can diagnose and provide counseling. The program also has extensive academic support and resources.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: The dress code is business casual or professional dress depending on the activity.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Office of Student Affairs & Admissions and Education Resources staff and faculty hold office hours and are available by appointment.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students will begin patient interaction in their first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Medical students learn through lectures, laboratories, patient simulations, and in patient-centered learning groups, where basic and clinical sciences are taught in the context of patient cases.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin approximately 20 months after matriculation.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: The Career & Life Instruction for Matriculation Building (CLIMB) program is a four-week program designed for incoming first year American Indian medical students.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Ranking is only used for the MSPE and it utilizes curricular assessments in Phase 2.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Phase 1 (20 months) 
Students learn basic and clinical sciences taught in the context of patient cases through lectures, laboratories, patient simulations and in patient-centered learning groups. 

Phase 2 (14 months)
Clinical experience in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Surgery, Psychiatry and Neuroscience. There are three different routes. 
1.Traditional: 8-week clerkships completed at home campus.
2.ROME (Rural Opportunities in Medical Education): Gain clinical  education experience by spending a half-year at rural health care sites including Devils Lake, Dickinson, Grafton, Hettinger, and Jamestown in ND and Benson, Bemidji, and Ortonville in MN.
3.MILE (Minot Integrated Longitudinal Experience): At the Minot campus, students experience different clerkship work each day and often see patients from treatment to prevention.

Phase 3 (12.5 months)
Clinical experience gained through a series of electives, acting internships and sub-internships.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: As a community-based medical college, primary care is the hub around which everything at UND’s School of Medicine & Health Sciences revolves. With emphases in Family and Internal Medicine, our curricula give young physicians, physician assistants, and other health providers the training they need to practice in a variety of settings, especially rural and underserved areas. Our School annually produces double the national average of family physicians and ranks in the 86th percentile for MD graduates entering Internal Medicine residencies—including residencies in North Dakota. Our Rural Opportunities in Medical Education (ROME) sends third-year students out to gain primary care experience in a rural practice setting, and our Indians Into Medicine (INMED) program is the nation’s top producer of American Indian physicians, most of whom enter the primary care fields.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Leader in Rural Health
The School leads the nation in rural health through the Center for Rural Health. It is designated as the North Dakota State Office of Rural Health, a federal-state partnership that helps rural communities build their health care services through collaborations and initiatives with a wide range of partners across the state. 

Cutting-Edge Lab Facilities and Educational Space
The SMHS building opened in 2016 and is designed to facilitate the education of an interprofessional health care workforce necessary for the health and vibrancy of North Dakota’s population. It features cutting-edge lab facilities and educational space designed to foster active and collaborative learning. 
Research focuses primarily on neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Parkinson’s Alzheimer’s), epigenetics and infectious disease (e.g., Zika, avian flu, Ebola).
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Our students do not have a traditional summer break, but have frequent breaks throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: A variety of community service activities are available through different student groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: There is a required epidemiology research project during third year, students may work alone or in small groups to complete the project.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: We have affiliation agreements for clinical education throughout the state and region.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine was established in 1905 as a basic science public medical school. In 1973, legislative action created an expanded curriculum and, in 1981, a full four-year community-integrated and university-based medical education program was instituted in the state. The School's name was changed in 1996 to the UND School of Medicine and Health Sciences to reflect the diversity of educational and research activities that occur at the School. The new medical school has been occupied since the summer of 2016.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The primary purpose of the University of North Dakota School of Medicine & Health Sciences is to educate physicians and other health professionals and to enhance the quality of life in North Dakota. Other purposes include the discovery of knowledge that benefits the people of this state and enhances the quality of their lives.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes, prior to matriculation and prior to clinical rotations.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: We require a response to an acceptance on the date of our Commit to Enroll deadline. Applicants accepted after May 2nd will have 48 hours to respond.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: A committee letter always counts as only two letters; an additional individual letter is required to meet the three-letter minimum. Letter packets count as three letters. If more than three letters are submitted the first three letters will be used. We follow AMCAS definitions of committee letters and letter packets.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Two of the letters should be from college instructors or faculty who know you well and can address your personal characteristics. The final letter should be from a supervisor (paid or volunteer) whom you have worked with and knows you well enough to speak to the characteristics. Who the letters are from is up to each applicant, but diversity is encouraged. Non-traditional applicants who have been out of school for a number of years may choose to include more letters from supervisors than faculty.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The interview day provides an important opportunity for applicants and members of the UND SMHS community to get to know each other. Current medical students conduct a Q & A on each interview day to answer applicant's questions.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: We begin sending interview invites in October for ND applicants and November through December for all other applicants.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews are conducted by a three-person team made up of admission committee members: an MD, a PhD and a medical student. One of the three members will take lead, but all three will ask questions.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Interviews take place during specific Fridays and Saturdays in October, November, December and January.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be conducted over Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Current legal residents of North Dakota who are first-time applicants to UND SMHS may apply through EDP.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Successful applicants must meet one of the residency preferences as defined on the UND SMHS admissions website. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents at the time of the application.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Preference to: current or former ND residents, ties to ND, MN , MT and WY (WICHE) residents, members of federally recognized tribes (INMED). We rarely have matriculants that do not meet one of these.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: All accepted applicants are required to attest to meeting these Standards of Capacity: https://med.und.edu/admissions/index.html
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our committee looks at the most recent total score and the break down of each of the four areas. If there are multiple attempts, they will assess the trend in the scores.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: We have a minimum MCAT of 495
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: All postbacc and graduate coursework will be considered for all applicants.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We do not have specific required prerequisite coursework. However, we do recommend courses to help prepare an applicant for the MCAT and the medical school curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We do not require a letter of intent, but applicants can email the admissions office to share that intent if they would like to.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Accepted applicants must complete the FAFSA to be considered for federal financial aid. In addition to federal aid, scholarships and institutional loans are available. 

RuralMed is a state-sponsored program designed to increase the number of physicians practicing in rural North Dakota. Students accepted for  RuralMed will have the cost of tuition paid for in return for practicing in rural North Dakota.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Accepted applicants are highly encouraged to select "Plan to Enroll" in the Choose Your Medical School Tools.
Accepted applicants at UND SMHS are required to select the "Commit to Enroll" option in AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tools. Failure to do so may result in the rescinding of the admissions offer.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: All applicants are notified of their position on the waitlist by January 31st. Updates will be sent every Friday until the cycle closes regardless of movement.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Entering medical students will demonstrate qualities aligned with competencies expected of medical students graduating from the UNDSMHS.

    An understanding of the natural science underpinnings of biomedical sciences including concepts of introductory-level biology, organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, physics, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology.
    An understanding of foundational concepts of psychology, sociology, and behavioral biology.
    Skill in scientific inquiry and reasoning, critical analysis, research methods, and statistics as applied to the natural, social, and/or behavioral sciences.
    Interpersonal and communication skills.
    Commitment to working with people of diverse cultures and socioeconomic status.
    Professionalism
    Adherence to ethical principles.
    Awareness and responsiveness to complex societal systems.
    Ability to function effectively within a team setting.
    Motivation to pursue lifelong learning.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have specific required prerequisite coursework. We require a bachelor's degree and it must be attained prior to matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
RESIDENCY
Preference for admissions is given to the following:
North Dakota legal residents
Applicants with North Dakota ties
WICHE applicants (currently limited to those from Montana and Wyoming)
INMED applicants (enrolled members of US federally recognized tribes)
Minnesota applicants, especially those from the Red River Valley

Applicants are encouraged to assess their suitability for the school based on the preference criteria. Those who meet the criteria are strongly encouraged to apply.

Please see the website for further details about the residency preferences and characteristics of a successful applicant: https://med.und.edu/admissions/student-affairs-admissions/prospective-students/residency-eligibility.html

UND rarely has matriculants that do not meet one of these residency preferences.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Although it is not a requirement to shadow a health care worker, it is strongly encouraged. We encourage applicants to shadow a broad spectrum of specialties, especially primary care. We also encourage applicants to gain shadowing experience in a rural area.
